thread:
maya: Noticed a p99 regress after the kernel switch when tool handlers return structured JSON and pause for external I/O. Figures attached below.
liam: hmm, is this the same workload as yesterday's KV stress test? :thinking:
sara: It's the chat endpoint with function calls + structured output. Breaks batching because stop-token comes late and we get many parked fn frames.
maya: Exactly. Profiling shows batch formation latency spikes at ~70ms -> 180ms at p99 after the new kernel pick logic.
perf-bot: perf snapshot: kernels=attn_v2,cuda_fused; avg_tok=4.2ms; p99_batch_wait=180ms; kv_cache_hits=0.86
liam: kv_cache_hits still high, so not cache miss. My suspicion: the continuous-batcher groups by soft budget then we hit tool-invoke pause so the head of batch stalls and kernel swaps thrash.
sara: I captured a short trace. Key bits: many batches form of size 12, decode loop hits `INVOKE_TOOL`, thread parks, other sequences stall waiting for prefix KV to sync.
maya: snippet of the problematic config we ran:
```yaml
batcher:
  policy: elastic_hold
  soft_budget_tokens: 256
  preempt_threshold: 0.25
  allow_prefetch_kv: true
  tool_coop_yield: false
```
liam: two ideas: 1) change policy to `interruptible` so parked requests don't block head-of-line, 2) mark function-invoke sequences as low-seq so they go into a secondary fast-path.
sara: also saw kernel selection flip mid-batch. The kernel picker chose a quantized kernel for tail tokens which increased per-token variance and made scheduling worse.
maya: can we get a run with `kernel_bias: prefer_stable` to avoid switching mid-batch? Also lower soft_budget to 128 and enable `kv_prefetch_on_invoke=true`
perf-bot: run queued: run_id=2026-03-18-2177; expected 30m.
liam: quick experiment results (10m sample):
- soft_budget=128, interruptible=true -> p99 batch_wait=72ms (-60%)
- kernel_bias=prefer_stable -> p99 kernel-swap-events down from 9/min to 1/min
- kv_prefetch_on_invoke=true -> observed ~40ms prefetch latency but reduced mid-batch stalls
maya: great. But prefetch adds cost and sometimes does extra KV work for calls that end up not invoking tool (false positives). Need thresholding.
sara: proposal: adaptive prefetch: only prefetch if predicted tool-likelihood > 0.6 and remaining_tokens > 32. Also mark structured-output stop token as a soft-terminator so batcher can close batch early when structured output starts.
liam: love adaptive prefetch. Model-side signal could be `tool_intent_score`. Where do we expose that? SDK + runtime header?
maya: SDK can send `X-Model-Intent: 0.72` in meta for now. Runtime will treat >0.6 as prefetch trigger.
perf-bot: canary run scheduled with adaptive prefetch + interruptible policy.
deploy-bot: canary deployed to pool-eta, policy=interruptible, kv_prefetch=adaptive, kernel_bias=prefer_stable.
sara: small gotcha: stop-tokens inside structured JSON sometimes appear mid-object, causing partial outputs and then tool-call detection misses them. We should treat the structured output grammar (e.g., begins with `{"tool_call":`) as an immediate delimiter.
liam: Agreed. I'll add a `structured_delim_regex` check in the decoder that short-circuits batch close when matched.
maya: next steps: liam to prototype decoder short-circuit + adaptive prefetch hook; sara to run cost/regression tests; I'll monitor p99 and unit cost.
liam: ETA for prototype PR: EOD tomorrow.
sara: I'll run perf harness after PR to validate p99 and token-cost delta.
maya: thanks team. If we see regressions on other workloads we roll back kernel_bias and keep interruptible + adaptive prefetch. :thumbsup:
liam: one-liner reminder command to reproduce the trace:
```bash
./tools/perf-run --workload=chat-toolcall-structured 
  --batcher.policy=interruptible 
  --batcher.soft_budget_tokens=128 
  --runtime.kernel_bias=prefer_stable 
  --kv.prefetch=adaptive
```
maya: dropping trace files into `/perf/traces/2177770001/` for anyone who wants them.
